U.S. EPA ENERGY STAR guide (Document Number 430-R-13-009) prepared for the United States Government, with the standard U.S. Government disclaimer; funded by U.S. EPA (Contract EP-BPA-12-H-0012) and begun under U.S. DOE Contract DE-AC02-05CH11231; no copyright or reuse terms printed.

Worrell, E., Kermeli, K. and Galitsky, C. (2013). Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Cement Making: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Document Number 430-R-13-009, August 2013 (limited update of the March 2008 version; file reformatted 2014-11-19). No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 5; front matter in roman numerals). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue: nearly every number is reprinted from other sources (ECRA 2009, Hollingshead and Venta 2009, Cembureau 1997, Holderbank 1993...), named at the end of each note. The guide writes ton = short ton and tonne = metric ton; per-ton values are converted to per tonne with an explicit formula (MBtu/ton x 1.055056/0.907185 = GJ/t; kWh/ton / 0.907185), printed metric values are used where the guide prints them. Main file: Table 2 2009 U.S. baseline (kiln feed preparation per t raw material, wet and dry clinker production fuel (HHV) and electricity per t clinker, finish grinding per t cement) with calcination CO2 0.51 t/t clinker; raw-material crushers and mills (incl. TXI plant before/after); coal mills (Cembureau, MPS by fuel); kiln types (wet, long dry, 3-6 stage preheater from Table 1, precalciner, best precalciner); clinker coolers (efficiency, conversion capex); waste-heat power (steam Rankine, ORC, Kalina capex; Indian 8 MW plant); finish mills (ball, VRM, ring roller, Horomill, HPGR, combined circuits, Table 5 configurations); advanced technologies (fluidized bed kiln, geopolymer, belite clinker, Aether). Flows: raw meal per t clinker, clinker per t cement (USGS 2008 conversion factors), electricity output of waste-heat power per t clinker (per short ton, unconverted). _measures.csv: every row of Tables 8 (dry) and 9 (wet), savings per short ton cement as printed (one row per fuel/electricity saving), payback as printed, investment cost from the Sect. 6 text added to the first row of each measure. _other-values.csv: Table 2 primary energy, totals and carbon columns, sector statistics, alternative ranges, Table 5 HPGR shares, Table 7 kiln-feed substitutes, percentages for advanced technologies. Not loaded: plant-wide cross-cutting measure details (motors, compressed air, fans, lighting; only their Table 8/9 rows), energy-management text, figures 1-10 (charts only), NOx values, and costs without a technology. All costs: price year not stated, publication year 2013 used; most cost figures come from 1993-2010 sources.

(1) Table 2 finish grinding SEC (61.6 / 53.7 kWh/st) disagrees with the text p.18 (60 / 52 kWh/st; 66 / 57 kWh/t); Table 2 loaded. (2) Table 1 (ECRA 2009) does not say whether the preheater kilns have precalciners, and gives no heating-value basis (ECRA normally LHV); Table 2 is explicitly HHV. (3) Many Sect. 6 numbers are printed per ton without saying short or metric, including reprinted European figures (e.g. Table 5 from Aydogan et al. 2006) that are probably per metric tonne; the guide convention (ton = short ton) was applied. (4) Wash mill: 5-7 kWh/ton stated first as consumption and then as reduction. (5) Grate cooler opex printed as $0.5-0.2/ton (reversed). (6) Investment costs printed both per ton and per annual ton clinker; per-ton units kept as printed. (7) Text typos: Schneinder for Schneider, Bolwek for Bolwerk, Holdebank, Pavillion/Pavilion; Table 8 row Use of Fly Ash, Blast Furnace Slag in Clinker (15% truncated; Table 3 lists Conversion to modern grate cooler and Optimize grate coolers twice in the dry column. (8) Scrap tire calorific value printed 14,000 Btu/ton (should be per lb). (9) LSF CO2 decrease printed 35-26 kg CO2/tonne (reversed).
